motivation: Cross-sectional exotic/native milkweed stage odds exhibit seasonal Simpson reversal; species identity among native hosts appears important. Test whether species identity predicts future observed late-instar occurrence beyond egg input, season, patch size and elapsed survey time using actual repeat-visit panels.
study_unit: Repeat surveys at same exact Route + Address_comp + Milkweed_sp; aggregate multiple within-date records to one host-species address-day observation; next chronological visit of same key only, without cross-year transitions.
outcome: Any 4th/5th-instar larvae at next visit 10-35 days after index survey; cross-sectional stage count, NOT tracked-individual survival.
species_selection: Species with >=100 qualifying 2022 repeat-visit transitions, based only on observation frequency not on target outcomes.
inclusion: Eggs and instars 4 and 5 nonnegative numeric
Index and next visit both same year
Exact Route/Address_comp/Milkweed_sp keys with correct species label

contrast.new_model: identical features plus four-species one-hot identity instead of botanical origin
contrast.model: L2 penalized logistic regression sklearn liblinear C=1, fixed settings, no tuned hyperparameters
contrast.test_metric: Log loss of next-visit late-instar presence (lower better)

validation.route_holdout: Leave one 2022 survey route out, train on remaining routes and predict complete held-out route; aggregate predictions across held-out routes
validation.temporal_holdout: Train 2022 only, predict 2023 same four species and same revisit rules, using no fitted hyperparameters from 2023
validation.bootstrapping: 4999 resamples of 2022 routes with replacement on frozen held-out predictions; 95% CI for reference-minus-new log loss, routes are units

gate: Species identity improves route-heldout 2022 log loss with route bootstrap 95% CI fully above zero AND improves 2023 temporal-heldout log loss. Otherwise do not promote the identity-specific ecological prediction.
caveats: This is an exploratory follow-up to a previously observed host species effect, not genuinely preregistered inference.
Monarch eggs and late larvae 10-35 days later are NOT matched individuals; larval stages could come from new eggs, movement, or repeated plant observations.
Addresses are imperfect patch identifiers and double rows on a date will be aggregated.
A logistic probability of later-stage detections conflates reproduction, predation, detection, weather, morphology and garden management.
2023 and 2024 sample sizes and seasonal coverage differ; do not compare naïvely as full replications.
No species-specific trait cause, demographic survival or fitness.
No p-value from treating repeated patch records as independent; 2022 route-cluster bootstrap only.
